title: Volcan: hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff

narration_audio.note: Filled in from the measured run. See video/README.md.

title_lines: Hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff.
A local run of commit {sha7}. Simulated Alexa+ front end. GitHub dry run.
outro_lines: Local run of commit {sha7}. Not the public deployment. Not an Alexa skill.
GitHub review: a dry run, recorded and not sent. Engine: local heuristic.
Product voice: the page's own sentences, rendered with the Windows system voice.

beats.narration_text: This is Volcan. A screen reader reads a patch one plus sign at a time. Volcan turns it into sound, speech and Braille, with one key press. Listen.
beats.speech_text: This is Volcan. A screen reader reads a patch one plus sign at a time. Volcan turns it into sound, speech and Braille, with one key press. Listen.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-09-28 against a local server on port 8871 with no cloud credentials: 18.13 s from the Enter press to the browser's speech end event in a rehearsal (earcon playing at 0.20 s, speech start 1.39 s, speech 16.74 s) and 18.15 s in a full rehearsal take. The passing 2026-09-27 take on a loaded machine measured 18.95 s. 19.5 s leaves 0.55 s over the slowest, and keeps the silence after the product's sentence short. video/capture-local.py fails the take if speech has not ended inside this window.
beats.visual_action: The companion page at first paint: the heading Hear your code review instead of scrubbing a diff, For blind and low-vision developers, the Inverted admin check patch, the silent preview (grey waveform, Falling contour, the finding sentence, Server's first sentence, not played yet) and the label Live MCP server, simulated Alexa+ front end. Not an Alexa skill. GitHub: dry-run. On the third sentence Alt and 1 puts the focus ring on Hear this code review; Enter after the narrator stops. The narrator is silent while the page plays the earcon WAV the server returned and the browser speaks the server's sentence, finding first. After the earcon ends the page scrolls so the earcon, the sentence, the security finding and the Braille share the frame while the words light.

beats.narration_text: The earcon came first, so the verdict arrived before the sentence. This patch touches security, so the cue falls; a clean patch gets a rising cue. The sentence opens with the finding itself. The engine meter reads local heuristic, because this run has no cloud credentials, and the round trip was measured in this browser.
beats.speech_text: The earcon came first, so the verdict arrived before the sentence. This patch touches security, so the cue falls; a clean patch gets a rising cue. The sentence opens with the finding itself. The engine meter reads local heuristic, because this run has no cloud credentials, and the round trip was measured in this browser.
beats.visual_action: The stage as the press left it, scrolled so the earcon, the spoken sentence, the security finding box and the first Braille cells share the frame: the waveform in its heard colour, the Falling contour, the earcon caption naming SECURITY_FINDING and 0.60 seconds of 16-bit PCM at 22050 Hz. On the last sentence the information button beside Synthesis engine opens the server's reason: no AWS credentials were resolved by the boto3 credential chain.

beats.narration_text: Now a real pull request, read from GitHub without a token. Alt and 6 jumps to the address box, and Enter opens it. The page outlines the next steps; ask for the findings. Listen.
beats.speech_text: Now a real pull request, read from GitHub without a token. Alt and six jumps to the address box, and Enter opens it. The page outlines the next steps; ask for the findings. Listen.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-09-28 against a local server on port 8871, after opening octocat/Hello-World pull request 1: 7.47 s in a rehearsal and 7.46 s in a full rehearsal take, from the click on Findings to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. 9.0 s leaves 1.5 s of margin. video/capture-local.py fails the take if speech has not ended inside this window.
beats.visual_action: Talk through a real pull request. Alt and 6 focuses the pull request URL box, the URL of octocat/Hello-World pull request 1 is typed and Enter opens it: the dialogue answers Opened octocat/Hello-World pull request 1 ... head commit 7044a8a ... 0 security findings. The page speaks that answer too; it is not in the recording, and a label in the caption band says so for exactly that stretch. The view moves to the dialogue and the outlined next steps, File by file, Findings and Read the lines. Findings after the narrator stops: the page plays its cue and speaks Understood: findings. No security finding in this change. That product voice is in the mix and captioned as Volcan.

beats.narration_text: Request changes stages the review, bound to the head commit Volcan read, under a single-use grant, and outlines Confirm. Nothing leaves until you say it. Confirm, and listen.
beats.speech_text: Request changes stages the review, bound to the head commit Volcan read, under a single-use grant, and outlines Confirm. Nothing leaves until you say it. Confirm, and listen.
beats.product_sound_basis: Measured on 2026-09-28 against a local server on port 8871, each time after Request changes on octocat/Hello-World pull request 1: 22.1 s and 21.8 s in two rehearsals and 21.96 s in a full rehearsal take, from the click on Confirm to the browser's speech end event for its readback and answer. 23.5 s leaves 1.4 s over the slowest. video/capture-local.py fails the take if speech has not ended inside this window.
beats.visual_action: A comment that says it is a dry-run demo goes into the comment box and Request changes stages the review: the dialogue reads back Ready to request changes ... bound to head commit 7044a8a, and Confirm and Cancel are outlined. The page speaks that readback too; it is not in the recording, and a label says so until Confirm interrupts it. Confirm after the narrator stops: the page plays its cue and speaks Understood: confirm. Dry run. Nothing was sent to GitHub. The head commit is still 7044a8a, and the exact request Volcan would send has been recorded. A live send would be refused: no GITHUB_TOKEN is set. That product voice is in the mix and captioned as Volcan. Midway the view moves to the review pane: Outcome recorded and not sent, and the exact POST request the server recorded.

beats.narration_text: Under the page is Volcan's Model Context Protocol server, written by hand to revision 2025-11-25. This button runs a real handshake: the negotiated version, a session identifier, and all twelve tools with their schemas.
beats.speech_text: Under the page is Volcan's Model Context Protocol server, written by hand to revision twenty twenty-five, eleven, twenty-five. This button runs a real handshake: the negotiated version, a session identifier, and all twelve tools with their schemas.
beats.visual_action: In Evidence, tab Server and MCP, press Run a real MCP handshake on the second sentence and hold on the four facts (2025-11-25, volcan-accessible-forge 0.1.0, the session id from the Mcp-Session-Id header, 12 tools), then expand the first tool to show its published inputSchema.

beats.narration_text: On this commit, 725 tests pass, and 23 of 23 protocol conformance checks. This button replays Amazon's documented Alexa+ requests as three clients; all three are served. Alexa+ itself has never called Volcan. Volcan: code review by ear and by touch.
beats.speech_text: On this commit, seven hundred and twenty-five tests pass, and twenty-three of twenty-three protocol conformance checks. This button replays Amazon's documented Alexa plus requests as three clients; all three are served. Alexa plus itself has never called Volcan. Volcan: code review by ear and by touch.
beats.visual_action: Evidence, tab Server and MCP: SERVER REACHED with the commit and the model path the server reported for this run. Press Replay the documented Alexa+ requests and hold on the three client lines and 3 of 3 clients served. Back to the connection strip and the Alexa+ box, which reads package built and tested locally, not certified or deployed, then close on the page heading and the Live MCP server, simulated Alexa+ front end label. The test and conformance counts are stated, not filmed.
